No. 1650.

SHANGHAI, 24th May 1937.

Sir,

Further to my letter of July 30th, 1936, No. 2748 (your
number D. 4836 of July 31st, 1936), I have the honour to inform
you that according to an article in the "Pester Lloyd" of May
1st 1937, the Vienna Police informed the Police at Budapest
that they had arrested a person, who called himself Dr. Bela
Szentivanyi and who most probably was a Yugoslavian citizen.
He posed as a doctor of a Chinese Mission, could produce however
no diploma and was found in possession of a pharmaceutical
chemist's diploma issued at New York, which has no value in
Europe. It was established that Szentivanyi's real name was
Julius Turcsany, 47 years of age, of Jewish confession, born in
Kassa. He was staying lately on the Semmering and in Schottwien,
where he tried to induce women and girls to join a mission in-
tended to be sent out to India. The Police at Budapest were
able to establish that Turcsany was sentenced ten years ago twice
on account of fraud and was known as a swindler then.

From a note in my files I find that Dr. (?) Szentivanyi
left Shanghai for Europe by the s. s. "Conte Verde" on August
22nd, 1936, and that before leaving he obtained a complete
dentist's outfit from a Japanese firm, which he took with him,
without having paid therefor.

He travelled disguised as a priest and it is rumoured
that he carried with him a consignment of drugs which he in-
tended to smuggle into Europe.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
〔签名〕
Consul.

Major K. M. Bourne,
Officer i/c Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

PAUL KOMOR.

SHANGHAI, 28th April 1936.

No. 589.

Sir,

Re: Dr. Adalbert (Béla) Szentiványi
384 Avenue de Roi Albert.

Although Dr. Szentiványi claims to be a Yugoslav subject, his person is of interest from the Hungarian point of view, because of his Hungarian name and Hungarian birth and also because, in general he passes as a Hungarian everywhere.

There were reasons why I doubted the bona fides of Dr. Szentivanyis right to the title of a medical doctor. He has, to the best of my knowledge, no diploma. He stated to me that, in his sudden flight from Yogoslavia some 5 years ago, all his papers and documents were left behind and lost. He has stated to some, that he obtained his diploma in Klausenburg (Transylvania,) Kassa (Northern-Hungary) and Budapest. Inquiries in Budapest have established the fact, that there is no record of a Dr. Szentiványi and the name is entirely unknown. The absence of a diploma is also documented by the fact, that Dr. Szentiványi is not on the Register of Physicians of the Municipal Council and is not admitted to practice in the Municipal Hospitals.

Inspite of this, Dr. Szentiványi was engaged as Physician by the Belgian Mission some three years ago and sent to Siu-Yuan, where he was stationed until the summer of 1934. He practiced at the Sacred Heart Hospital in Yangtzepoo until October 1934 and performed there operations in, as I have been informed, an entirely unorthodox and unprofessional manner. He then went to Europe, but failed to go to Hungary owing to, as he said, Yugoslavs being refused Visas at that time. He was in Geneva with some formula which he has "discovered" against the Opium habit. He was in Rome, where he was received in audience by the Pope and received a Papal decoration which was bestowed upon him on the recommendation of the Mission Prokurator at Siu-Yuan. He alleges to have been at Stennockerzell and to have been received by His Majesty the King of Hungary.

He returned to Shanghai at the end of 1934 or beginning of 1935. Allegedly, he deals in Medicines which he sells to the Missions. On the otherhand, I am informed that in the summer of 1935 the Missions, in a notice published in the Journal de Shanghai, explicitly stated, that they have no connection with Dr. Szentiványi.

I

W. G. Boissevain, Esquire,
Consul-General for The Netherlands,

SHANGHAI.

上海，1936年4月28日。

第 589 号。

先生：

事由：阿达尔伯特（贝拉）·森特伊万尼博士
阿尔伯特国王大道384号。

虽然森特伊万尼博士声称是南斯拉夫臣民，但由于他的匈牙利姓名、匈牙利出生地，以及他通常在各地都自称匈牙利人，因此从匈牙利角度来看，此人值得关注。

我有理由怀疑森特伊万尼博士拥有医学博士头衔的正当性。据我所知，他没有文凭。他对我说，大约5年前他突然从南斯拉夫逃亡时，所有文件和证件都遗留并丢失了。他对一些人声称，他在克劳森堡（特兰西瓦尼亚）、卡萨（北匈牙利）和布达佩斯获得了文凭。在布达佩斯的查询证实，没有森特伊万尼博士的记录，该名字完全无人知晓。没有文凭的事实也体现在以下情况：森特伊万尼博士不在工部局的医师注册名单上，也不被允许在工部局医院执业。

尽管如此，森特伊万尼博士大约在三年前被比利时传教团聘为医生，并被派往绥远（Siu-Yuan），他在那里任职直到1934年夏天。他在杨树浦的圣心医院行医直到1934年10月，据我获悉，他在那里进行手术的方式完全非正统且不专业。随后他前往欧洲，但因他说当时南斯拉夫人被拒发签证而未能前往匈牙利。他在日内瓦带着一种他“发现”的对抗鸦片瘾的配方。他在罗马，受到教皇接见，并获得了一枚由绥远传教团 procurator 推荐授予他的教皇勋章。他声称曾在斯滕诺克泽尔（Stennockerzell），并受到匈牙利国王陛下的接见。

他于1934年底或1935年初返回上海。据称，他从事向传教团出售药品的生意。另一方面，我获悉，1935年夏天，各传教团在《上海日报》刊登的公告中明确声明，他们与森特伊万尼博士没有任何关系。

我

W. G. 布瓦瑟万 先生，
荷兰总领事，

上海。

- 2 -

I consider that Dr.Szentiványi's person ought to be of
interest to the authorities and it would, I think, be useful
to make official inquiries of the State Police of Budapest
in order to establish his real identity.

It is contrary to Hungarian interests, that a person should
call himself a Doctor, without a degree from a Hungarian Uni-
versity, if such is not the case and it is contrary to local
public interest that any such person should have the possibility
of practicing medicine privately.

I might add that amongst the Hungarian Community here
considerable doubt exists as to the means whereby Dr.Szentiványi
earns a living, and, because these doubts have been expressed
quite frequently of late I consider it necessary now to bring
the matter to your notice for such action as you may consider to
be necessary or justified in the circumstances.

I might add, that the information herein contained has
been communicated to me in part by Dr.Szentiványi himself and
in part by third persons. Personally, I have had very little
contact with him, especially during the past 18 months and
I have no personal knowledge of his activities.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

(sd.) Paul Komor.

Sir,

Re Dr. Adalbert (Béla) Szentivanyi
384 Avenue du Roi Albert

Although Dr. Szentivanyi claims to be a Yugoslav subject, his person is of interest from the Hungarian point of view, because of his Hungarian name and Hungarian birth and also because, in general he passes as a Hungarian everywhere.

There were reasons why I doubted the bona fides of Dr. Szentivanyis right to the title of a medical doctor. He has, to the best of my knowledge, no diploma. He stated to me that, in his sudden flight from Yugoslavia some 5 years ago, all his papers and documents were left behind and lost. He has stated to some that he obtained his diploma in Klausenburg (Transylvania) Kassa (Northern Hungary) and Budapest. Inquiries in Budapest have established the fact, that there is no record of a Dr. Szentivanyi and the name is entirely unknown. The absence of a diploma is established the fact, that there is no record of a Dr. Szentivanyi and the name is entirely unknown. The absence of a diploma is also documented by the fact, that Dr. Szentivanyi is not on the Register of Physicians of the Municipal Council and is not admitted to practice in the Municipal Hospitals.

Inspite of this, Dr. Szentivanyi was engaged as Physician by the Belgian Mission some three years ago and sent to Siu-Yuan, where he was stationed until the summer of 1934. He practiced at the Sacred Heart Hospital in Yangtzepoo until October 1934 and performed there operations in, as I have been informed, an entirely unorthodox and unprofessional manner. He then went to Europe, but failed to go to Hungary owing, to, as he said, Yugoslavs being refused visas at that time. He was in Geneva with some formula which he has "discovered" against the Opium habit. He was in Rome, where he was received in audience by the Pope and received a Papal decoration which was bestowed upon him on the recommendation of the Mission Procurator at Siu-Yuan. He alleges to have been at Stennockerzell and to have been received by His Majesty The King of Hungary.

He returned to Shanghai at the end of 1934 or beginning of 1935. Allegedly, he deals in medicines which he sells to the Missions. On the other hand, I am informed that in the summer of 1935 the Missions, in a notice published in the Journal de Shanghai, explicitly stated, that they have no connection with Dr. Szentivanyi.

I consider that Dr. Szentivanyi's person ought to be of interest to the authorities and it would, I think, be useful to make official inquiries of the State Police of Budapest in order to establish his real identity.

It is contrary to Hungarian interests, that a person should call himself a Doctor, without a degree from a Hungarian University, if such is not the case and it is contrary to local public interest that any such person should have the possibility of practicing medicine privately.

I might add that amongst the Hungarian Community here considerable doubt exists as to the means whereby Dr. Szentivanyi earns a living, and, because these doubts have been expressed quite frequently of late, I consider it necessary now to bring the matter to your notice for such action as you may consider to be necessary or justified in the circumstances.

尽管桑蒂瓦尼博士声称自己是南斯拉夫臣民，但由于其匈牙利姓氏、出生于匈牙利，以及他通常在各地都被视为匈牙利人，因此从匈牙利的角度来看，他这个人值得关注。

我有理由怀疑桑蒂瓦尼博士拥有医学博士头衔的合法性。据我所知，他没有文凭。他向我陈述，在大约5年前突然逃离南斯拉夫时，他的所有文件和证件都遗留并丢失了。他曾对某些人声称，他在克劳森堡（Klausenburg，特兰西瓦尼亚）、卡萨（Kassa，匈牙利北部）和布达佩斯获得了文凭。在布达佩斯的查询已证实，没有桑蒂瓦尼博士的记录，该名字完全无人知晓。没有文凭这一事实也已得到证实，即没有桑蒂瓦尼博士的记录，且该名字完全无人知晓。此外，桑蒂瓦尼博士不在工部局医师注册名册上，也不获准在工部局医院执业，这也证明了他缺乏文凭。

尽管如此，桑蒂瓦尼博士大约在三年前被比利时传教会聘为医生，并被派往绥远（Siu-Yuan），他在那里驻留至1934年夏季。他在杨树浦的圣心医院（Sacred Heart Hospital）行医直至1934年10月，据我获悉，他在那里进行手术的方式完全非正统且不专业。随后他前往欧洲，但据他说，由于当时南斯拉夫人被拒发签证，他未能前往匈牙利。他在日内瓦，带着一种他“发现”的对抗鸦片瘾的配方。他在罗马，受到教皇接见，并获得了一枚教皇勋章，该勋章是根据绥远传教会监牧的推荐授予他的。他声称曾在斯泰诺克泽尔（Stennockerzell），并受到匈牙利国王陛下接见。

他于1934年底或1935年初返回上海。据称，他从事药品交易，将其出售给各传教会。另一方面，我获悉，1935年夏季，各传教会在《上海日报》（Journal de Shanghai）上刊登公告，明确声明他们与桑蒂瓦尼博士没有任何关系。

我认为桑蒂瓦尼博士其人应引起当局的关注，而且我认为，向布达佩斯国家警察进行正式查询以查明其真实身份将是有益的。

With reference to the letter dated May 4, 1933 from Dr.
Paul Horner of "Hungarian Relief Fund" Shanghai, regarding one Laszlo
Walter alias Laszlo Waller, enquiries show that Laszlo Waller is a
Hungarian subject, born on July 17, 1896 at Budapest, Hungary and
is a musician by profession. During the Great War he served in the
Austro-Hungarian Army. In 1915 Waller was taken prisoner in Russia
and was sent to Siberia. In 1918 he married at Krasnoyarsk, Siberia,
one Marsela Ivanovna Nitetska, a Russian woman of Polish origin. He
has a daughter named Eleonora, about 15 years of age. It is reported
that Laszlo Waller's proper name is Laszlo Walla, and that he changed
it to Waller before leaving Russia.

In the early part of 1927 Waller together with his family
left Vladivostok for Shanghai from 1927 till 1925 he was employed
as a violinist with various restaurants and cinemas in this city.
In 1925 Waller left for Hankow and remained there till 1927 when,
owing to the anti-foreign movement, he returned to Shanghai. In
Hankow he earned his living as a musician, from 1927 till April
1933 he was employed as a musician at the Pantheon Theatre, and
other places. His last place of employment was the Sheikh Cabaret
111/13 Avenue Edward 7. Recently he left Shanghai for Chefoo where
he is present employed with the "Silver Dollar" Cabaret cabaret in
the capacity of musician.

His wife and daughter are now residing at No. 88 Route
Vallon, House No. 11 Telephone No. 84369.

1927年初，瓦勒携家人离开符拉迪沃斯托克前往上海。从1927年至1925年[原文如此，疑为1927-1930或类似时间段，但依原文翻译]，他在本市的多家餐馆和电影院担任小提琴手。1925年，瓦勒前往汉口，并在那里停留至1927年，后因排外运动返回上海。在汉口，他以音乐家为生。从1927年至1933年4月，他在万神殿剧院（Pantheon Theatre）及其他场所受雇为音乐家。他最后的工作地点是位于爱德华七世路（Avenue Edward 7）111/13号的谢赫歌舞厅（Sheikh Cabaret）。最近他离开上海前往烟台，目前在“银元”歌舞厅（"Silver Dollar" Cabaret cabaret）担任音乐家。

他的妻子和女儿目前居住在法租界华伦路（Route Vallon）88号11室，电话号码84369。
